pairs.subject: translation-pipeline-topology
pairs.evidence: lib/i18n/request.ts:15 The request config loads only the selected locale's catalog and sets neither a merge with the canonical cs catalog nor a getMessageFallback, so a key missing from en.json shows next-intl's raw key path plus an error, not the canonical Czech unit. Measured 2026-11-04: cs and en both have 3215 keys and 0 are missing, so the gap is latent today rather than visible to readers.

techniques.evidence: lib/i18n/request.ts:15 No per-unit fallback to the defaultLocale catalog; a miss becomes the 'blank or error on miss' failure the technique names. The cs path is unchanged (same single import), so the canonical path carries no i18n tax.
lib/i18n/config.ts:8 One registry holds the codes, endonyms (localeNames) and short labels, and isLocale validates against it. request.ts, locale.ts, useFormat.ts and the switcher all read it.

pairs.evidence: features/landing/messages.test.ts:68 The landing catalog gate checks key parity, placeholder parity and non-emptiness for all 105 landing keys, but compares values against the cs source for only the 12 denik.* keys, with no committed allowlist. So parity stands in as the coverage claim for the other 93 keys. Measured 2026-11-04: only landing.nav.index and landing.nav.data are identical today.

techniques.evidence: features/landing/messages.test.ts:68 Parity is gated for the whole namespace. The value comparison at line 127 (not.toEqual) covers only the denik.* subset and has no allowlist of values that may legitimately match.
features/landing/serverIntl.ts:34 The server-side landing intl resolves the locale through the shared registry (isLocale/defaultLocale) instead of keeping its own list.
